To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cardiac NGF overexpression induces bone marrow–derived progenitor cells mobilization and homings to the injured myocardia.
NGF overexpression induces the release of BM-derived PCs, which are recruited to the injured heart and contribute to the repair process.
NGF-GT promotes cardiac repair following MI in mice through activation of osteoblasts, osteoclasts, and MMP9 and mobilization and hominge of BM-derived progenitor cells to the infarcted heart.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular pathways underlying the reparative response of PCs in the infarcted myocardium.
the mechanisms by which NGF-GT promotes cardiac repair after MI, and it is expected that the knowledge gained may lead to novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of cardiac diseases.
the mechanisms of cardiac repair and regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NGF is a key player in the BM-derived PCs mobilizing/homing process, and this is an essential step for cardiac repair following MI.
NGF-GT promotes the reparative process in the ischemic myocardium by enhancing the mobilization/homing of BM-derived PCs.
NGF-GT promotes cardiac repair by increasing the number of PCs and enhancing their migration to the infarcted heart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NGF-GT promotes the reparative process by enhancing PCs homing, which is dependent upon the activation of osteoclastic activity and the release of MMP9.
NGF is a potent inducer of BM-derived PCs mobilizing and homing to infarcted heart.
NGF is a key player in BM-derived PCs activation and mobilization to the injured myocardial tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NGF-GT enhances the BM-derived PCs mobilizing/homing response to ischemia.
NGF-GT induces BM-derived PCs mobilizations/homing and that these processes are dependent on MMP9.

NGF-GT induces the activation of the endogenous osteoclasts in the BM and the expression of the MMP9 in the BM, which in turn promote the detachment of PCs from the BM endostal niche and their liberation to the circulation.
